citations.field: 備(备) headword, form sequence and explanation; source-scan image
citations.text: The inspected page is headed 備(备), bèi. The author calls the graph phonosemantic and quotes the received Shuowen analysis “備，慎也。从人，[unidentified printed phonetic graph]聲.” The author interprets the early graph as a person carrying an arrow container, calls the container graph the original graph for 箙, and connects the image with guarding/preparation. The text describes graphic change from the Western Zhou through Warring States and seal forms, then says the later regular graph retained 人 while its sound-bearing structure became obscured. It describes the simplified form 备 as selected from a cursive form of the sound element and fixed as a whole graph, losing the visible phonosemantic structure. The sequence labels are 商; 商; 西周; 西周; 戰國; 《說文》小篆; 漢; 漢; 漢; 楷書, with printed glyphs p001–p004 left unidentified. These are the author’s claims, not independently dated attestations or verified readings of the rare graph. The page’s account ends before the next headword 儈; no continuation of the 備 account appears on this page.

citations.field: 備(备) headword; form sequence and explanation; directly inspected source scan
citations.text: I directly inspected the attached scan. The headword is 備(备), bèi. The prose says the early graph is a person carrying a container, describes graphic changes, and states that simplified 备 was selected from a cursive form of the sound element and fixed as a whole graph. The scan does not identify that cursive form as today’s 夂 or 田. Four numbered glyph occurrences in the displayed sequence remain unresolved from the scan; they should stay occurrence-specific and must not be normalized to 葡, 蒲, 夂, 田, or 𤰈. The printed page’s 備 discussion ends before the next headword 儈.

citations.text: The headword on printed p. 705 is 備(备), bèi. The entry calls 備 a phonosemantic character, says its early form depicts a person carrying a container, and describes the sound-bearing part as undergoing the greatest change. It says the later regular 備 retained 人, and that simplified 备 took the sound element’s cursive form as the whole graph. The scan does not identify that cursive form as 夂 or 田. Four numbered forms in the sequence and the rare printed graph in the quoted Shuowen analysis remain unresolved from the pixels; they are not normalized here. The account ends on this page before the separate headword 位.
